sourceTitle: Memoirs of Extraordinary Popular Delusions and the Madness of Crowds
description: "Memoirs of Extraordinary Popular Delusions and the Madness of Crowds" by Charles Mackay is an early study of crowd psychology first published in 1841. This journalistic work examines humanity's susceptibility to collective manias through three volumes exploring financial bubbles, religious crusades, witch trials, alchemy, and countless other follies.
longDescription: Source subjects: Social psychology; Swindlers and swindling; Impostors and imposture.
